title: Interactive Pattern Lab for Console Gestalt and Cost Controls
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Create an interactive pattern lab and component variant library that unifies gestalt rules (spacing, elevation, density) with cost-control UI patterns (budget chips, per-route rollouts, cost sparklines). Deliver a Figma library, token mapping guide, and a handoff package for engineering to adopt design tokens as code-ready JSON. Focus on predictable behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment views.
background: Current console components for cost and rollout controls were designed incrementally across features. Inconsistent spacing, motion timing, and token naming cause implementation drift and make runtime cost mappings ambiguous for engineers (e.g., card padding vs. metric chip density). This ticket consolidates those decisions into a pattern lab that can be consumed by Product, Eng, and Design.
goals: Define a small set of gestalt rules (grid, density, elevation) applicable across dashboards and rollout surfaces
Create Figma component variants for metric cards, budget chips, rollout toggles, and cost sparklines with accessible color tokens
Provide a token mapping guide that links visual tokens to runtime semantics (batching, cache-hit indicator, route-level cost multipliers)
Ship a consumable Figma library and a JSON token export for engineers to import into the console component repo
scope: Design system side: tokens, component variants, motion specs, and a pattern lab prototype. Engineering implementation and storybook integration will be delivered in a follow-up ENG ticket. Exclude backend cost-aggregation logic from this ticket.
deliverables: Figma pattern lab file with interactive demos (dashboard sample, rollout panel, cost inspector)
Component library: MetricCard (3 densities), BudgetChip (active/disabled/overflow), RolloutRail (canary/A-B/percent), CostSparkline (mini/expanded)
Token mapping doc (tokens -> suggested runtime keys) in Confluence
Design-to-engineer handoff bundle: tokens.json, component props table, motion timing spec
acceptance_criteria: Figma library is published and link shared with PM/Eng
Token mapping doc reviewed by an infra engineer and a PM with sign-off
Accessibility pass completed: contrast ratios, keyboard focus, and screenreader labeling for rollout controls
Prototype demonstrates consistent behavior across three example screens: hosted dashboard, dedicated capacity views, private deployment cost inspector
decisions: Adopt a 4-column density system (compact / default / comfortable / spacious) used across metric cards and rails
Use token aliasing for runtime mapping (visual.tokens.cardPadding -> runtime.tokens.ui.card_padding_ms) to avoid breaking engineering naming conventions
Favor subtle motion (120ms ease-out for state changes) to minimize perceived latency in cost updates
Use a separate semantic color palette for cost states (savings, neutral, overruns) rather than repurposing status colors to preserve existing incident/status language
design_notes: Prototype uses real production telemetry samples to populate sparklines and cost forecasts. For handoff, export tokens in both CSS/JS-friendly names and a machine-readable JSON. Include examples of how batching/cache-hit indicators can be surfaced as microinteractions (small badge with tooltip and latency breakdown). Document trade-offs between token granularity and engineering effort in the mapping guide.
